deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's systematic treatment of Hilbert–Schmidt (H.-S.) operators as the Hilbert tensor product. It belongs to the 1953 functional-analysis notes, a preparatory exposition alongside the nuclear/trace-class material that feeds into 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' (PTT) and the 'Résumé'.

(i) Definition 2 (from the previous page) is completed. The space of H.-S. operators E→F, written L^2(E,F) (or L^2(E) when F=E), carries the Hilbert structure transported from the Hilbert completion \bar E ⊗^{(2)} F. The H.-S. norm of u is ||u||_2. Since the injection \bar E ⊗^{(2)} F → L(E,F) has norm ≤1, one gets (16): ||u||_∞ ≤ ||u||_2.

(ii) H.-S. operators are compact; indeed they are norm limits in L(E,F) of finite-rank operators. They are exactly the operators whose matrix (u_ij) in orthonormal bases (e_i), (f_j) is square-summable, and then ||u||_2 = (Σ|u_ij|^2)^{1/2}. Hence \bar E ⊗^{(2)} F is identified with L^2(E,F).

(iii) Theorem, part 1 (ideal property): if u is H.-S., so are Au and uA for any bounded A, with (17) ||Au||_2 ≤ ||A|| ||u||_2 and ||uA||_2 ≤ ||A|| ||u||_2.

(iv) Part 2: u is H.-S. iff u* is, and then ||u||_2 = ||u*||_2. More precisely (18) (u,v) = (v*,u*). Thus u ↦ u* is an antiunitary map L^2(E,F) → L^2(F,E), i.e. a unitary from the conjugate space onto L^2(F,E). The next page derives this from the symmetry \bar E⊗F ≅ F⊗\bar E.

(v) Part 3 (spectral characterization): let h = √(u*u) with eigenvalues ρ_i. Then u is H.-S. iff Σρ_i^2 < ∞, and (19) ||u||_2 = ||h||_2 = (Σρ_i^2)^{1/2}. The proof on the next page uses the polar decomposition u = Uh, h = Vu with partial isometries U, V, together with part 1.

(vi) Corollary at the foot of the page: u is H.-S. iff u*u is of 'Fredholm' type (i.e. trace class/nuclear), and then ||u||_2 = √(Tr u*u) = √(||u*u||_1).

The purpose of all this is to set up the Hilbert-space model case (L^1 = projective, L^2 = Hilbert, L^∞ = injective tensor products) before the general theory of nuclear operators and tensor norms.
errors: No mathematical errors. Formula (18) (u,v) = (v*,u*) is correct: (u,v) = Tr(v*u) = Tr(uv*) = (v*,u*).
Gap in what is written on this page only: the compactness/finite-rank approximation statement is asserted here without proof.

ideas.what: Identification of the Hilbert tensor product \bar E ⊗^{(2)} F with the Hilbert–Schmidt operators, with ||u||_∞ ≤ ||u||_2
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert–Schmidt class S_2 as Hilbert tensor product
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), Ch. I/II discussion of Hilbert spaces; Résumé (1953/56)

ideas.modern_name: S_2 is a two-sided operator ideal; u ↦ u* isometric
ideas.where_published: standard; cf. Schatten 'A theory of cross-spaces' (1950)

ideas.where_published: PTT and Résumé (treatment of Hilbert-space case of nuclear operators)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but entirely standard exposition of Hilbert–Schmidt theory. The only mild historical interest is the terminology: he appears to call trace-class operators 'Fredholm', an early name before 'nucléaire' became standard. That is a known feature of his early writing.
transcription_corrections: Bottom line: the word after 'u*u' looks like 'Fredholm' (his early term for trace-class/nuclear), giving 'u H.-S. ⟺ u*u Fredholm, et alors ||u||_2 = √(Tr u*u) = √(||u*u||_1)'. It is preceded by an underlined heading, probably 'Corollaire'.

Lines 5–6 should read roughly: 'sont des applications compactes, et même limites dans L(E,F) d'applications de rang fini' — the remainder of that line and the next ('…F sont…', 'qui satisfont un op.…') are illegible scribble.
'Th. 3)' is item 3) of the same Theorem; 'Th.' is a marginal annotation, not a new theorem.
The left pencil marginal near item 3 plausibly reads '(Caractérisation spectrale)'.
Line 3 should read '$L^{(2)}(E,F)$' and line 4 '$u\in L^2(E,F)$ se note $\|u\|_2$'.
The struck-out passage under item 3) concerned the eigenvalues ρ_i of h; the retained text reads 'que l'on ait Σρ_i^2 < +∞. Alors'.
